purpose: Advance current synchronized branch from the v021 Mar-1943 rollback through 1943-09-30 after closing Aleutians, June Efate, Five-Go Phase II, India/Burma coastal-operation study, and Europe/Eastern Front Q3 synchronization.

overrides.effective_rule: Current synchronized analysis frontier is 1943-10-01T00:00. v021 1943-03-26 reopening has been closed through Sep 30; downstream Q4/1944 files remain provisional until revisited.

Use ALEUTIANS_ATTU_KISKA_REAUDIT_1943-03_07_SETTLEMENT_v001: no historical Komandorski battle central, Mar fast convoy reaches Attu, limited May rescue, Attu ends early Jun, Kiska evacuates late Jul. Do not auto-copy historical Komandorski/LANDCRAB outcomes.

Yamamoto survives 1943-04-18. Historical Operation Vengeance kill-chain is unavailable because high-grade COMINT precision and Guadalcanal/P-38 geometry differ. Yamamoto remains Combined Fleet commander through the current 1943 frontier unless later events change it.

Efate operation occurs Jun 8-9 as limited neutralization, not occupation or compulsory carrier duel. Wasp survives; first-line Japanese carrier group remains largely intact; Efate severe output suppression lasts days and below-full recovery about two weeks.

Do not cite a historical-scale Guadalcanal campaign as the source of Japanese logistics learning in this branch. Avoiding improvised escalating sustainment after overextension is a general anti-pattern visible from logistics accounting and other branch operations, not a Guadalcanal lesson.

India/Burma coastal operation is an advanced operational study/preparation-authorized option through Sep 30, not an execution GO. Cox's Bazar land-sea link is minimum success; Chittagong is conditional exploit; deep Calcutta/Assam advance is not automatic.

Air-drop/flying-boat delivery is small high-value field insurance only. Do not add it to sea/land throughput to make the Cox's sustainment gate pass. Persistent dependence on air supply is an AMBER/RED condition.

Historical Allied CBI/Burma intentions do not imply historical force allocation or schedule. British additional carrier losses, Mediterranean/Home Fleet competition, shipping/crew friction and US Pacific commitments must be paid. A rash British counteroffensive remains possible but low-probability unless readiness/command pressure supports it.

As US new fast-carrier groups become combat-ready, the Sep-end central India package allocates zero Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu/Soryu. They remain Pacific fleet-in-being; India must be designed around secondary carriers/base air/old BB/CA/DD/submarines unless a later Pacific gate reopens them.

Italian armistice starts a gradual RN release clock but does not free Mediterranean carrier/escort/landing resources immediately. Salerno, German occupation, Luftwaffe, convoy/escort and Home Fleet commitments continue; Eastern Fleet reinforcement becomes more plausible only gradually in Oct-Nov and remains conditional.
